_doc: Definite and indefinite articles, by noun class and number.
Keyed by ISO 639-3. A language listed here overrides what the translation
table yields; a language absent from it is derived as before.
Wiktionary translates `the` with one entry per gender and almost never
one per number, so the plural article was missing everywhere except
French: German said 'der' for a plural, Spanish 'el', Italian 'il',
Portuguese 'o'. It translates `one` rather than the article, so Italian
offered the citation form 'uno' and wrote 'uno cono' where 'un cono'
belongs, and Portuguese had no feminine at all and wrote 'um esfera'.
Keys are class.number, and a class of `-` matches any. Only languages
whose paradigm could be checked; a language whose article is a suffix
rather than a word -- Swedish, Romanian, the Scandinavian languages --
is not here, because the engine writes articles as separate tokens and
supplying one would put it in the wrong place.
The Scandinavian languages appear with an indefinite paradigm and no
definite one, which is not an oversight: their indefinite article is a free
word and their definite is a suffix on the noun. Writing the suffix here
would put it in front of the noun as a word of its own.
